newsitem.title: INDIA: Low mill buying halts Indian cotton gains.
newsitem.headline: Low mill buying halts Indian cotton gains.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Friday lost some of its recent gains owing to low mill buying and light profit-taking, dealers said.
"Recently new crop arrivals in the producing centres remained low due to severe cold weather but now arrivals have started picking up as temperatures are returning to normal," one broker said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 5/10 rupees to 810/860 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by five rupees to 1,415/1,635 rupees per maund.
F-414 fell by 20/30 rupees to 1,850/1,865 rupees per maund. Gujarat cotton however moved in a narrow range and finished on a quiet note. -- Bombay Commodities +91-22-265 9000
